card.title: Vectors and components
card.body: A **vector** is a quantity with both **magnitude** and **direction** (unlike a *scalar*, which has magnitude only). In two dimensions, a vector $\vec{A}$ at angle $\theta$ counterclockwise from the $+x$-axis splits into two perpendicular **components**: $A_x = A\cos\theta$ and $A_y = A\sin\theta$, with $A = \sqrt{A_x^2 + A_y^2}$ and $\tan\theta = A_y / A_x$ (for $A_x \neq 0$, checking the quadrant).
card.says: break any angled vector into an $x$-part and a $y$-part so you can add vectors along straight axes.
card.useWhen: forces, displacements, or velocities point at angles and you need to combine them or work along one axis at a time.
card.example: A vector of magnitude $A = 20\text{ N}$ at $\theta = 60^\circ$ above the $+x$-axis has $A_x = 20\cos 60^\circ = 10\text{ N}$ and $A_y = 20\sin 60^\circ = 10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$. Check: $\sqrt{10^2 + (10\sqrt{3})^2} = \sqrt{100 + 300} = 20\text{ N}$.
card.analogy: Giving directions on a city grid: instead of saying "walk diagonally", you give how many blocks east ($x$) and how many blocks north ($y$).
